concerns.text: The plan proceeds with a *placeholder CSV* because no verified HEA dataset is available (see “Critical data‑availability note”). Training and evaluation on synthetic, unverified data cannot support the research claim about real high‑entropy alloy predictive power, violating construct validity.

Uncertainty is quantified only by ensemble variance from Random Forest / Gradient Boosting models (Phase 2‑3.1‑3.3). Tree‑ensemble variance is not a calibrated predictive uncertainty metric and may not reflect true model confidence in extrapolation, undermining Principle VI (Extrapolation Integrity).

The Hold‑out Known set is created via a *non‑random* stratified split by element‑pair groups (Phase 0‑0.5). This deterministic split can introduce systematic bias and does not guarantee that the hold‑out truly represents out‑of‑distribution data, threatening the validity of the extrapolation error assessment.

The True Novel generation uses the same placeholder data to build a “Local Proxy Index” (Phase 0‑0.6) and then filters candidates against it. Because the index is derived from the same synthetic source, any leakage or overlap (e.g., hash collisions) may not be fully eliminated, confounding the novelty criterion.
